lastText: File ClosedThe Coup That Didn't TakeContestedItalian High Command, 1940–1945End of hostilities: SEPTEMBER 1943: SPECULATIVE · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathThis file closes on September 1943, a speculative branch's own ending rather than a date the documented record recognizes: six weeks of an Italian army fighting itself that the actual, bloodless transition of July 1943 never had to spend. The human cost of this path lands close to the historical record: a war that cost Italy its colonial empire, its monarchy within a year of the peace, and a divided memory of who actually fought whom in its final nineteen months. War was declared on Britain alone, months after France had already settled its own armistice without Italian participation: a different opening than the historical one, fought for the Mediterranean prize directly rather than for a seat at a peace table that no longer existed to claim. A speculative path with almost no historical footing: the officer corps' actual loyalty to the constitutional monarchy in July 1943 proved deeper than any loyalty to Mussolini personally. What this file records instead is a counterfactual crisis of legitimacy inside the regime's own institutions: one the losing war underneath it would have overtaken regardless of who signed the orders.
